s1.syndrome_frame: a gradually enlarging, red, cutaneous tumor with a hard nodule on the upper arm
salient_findings: red tumor on the right upper arm
key_facts: 16-year-old girl
previously healthy
lesion started as a small cutaneous nodule
enlarged over 6 months
no history of local trauma or insect bite
unremarkable personal, past, and family histories
6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red tumor
nontender, firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor
normal laboratory tests
normal physical and systemic examinations
multilocular spaces below the epidermis on pathological examination
solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance

shortlist.label: Pilomatrixoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of a firm, cutaneous nodule

shortlist.label: Dermatofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: possible given the hard nodule and cutaneous location

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to rapid growth and cutaneous presentation

shortlist.label: Pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the red, protuberant tumor

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the firm-to-hard nodule and cutaneous location

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: possible given the red color and cutaneous presentation

shortlist.label: Cavernous hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the multilocular spaces on pathological examination

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the large, protuberant tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of a firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor, multilocular spaces below the epidermis, and a solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance on pathological examination are characteristic of pilomatrixoma. Additionally, the basophilic cells and shadow cells seen on histological examination are typical of this condition.

rejected.label: Dermatofibroma
rejected.why: Dermatofibroma typically presents as a small, firm nodule and does not usually have the multilocular spaces or the characteristic basophilic and shadow cells seen in pilomatrixoma.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Keratoacanthoma often has a central crater-like depression and typically resolves on its own, which does not match the description of the lesion in the vignette.

rejected.label: Pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: Pyogenic granuloma is usually smaller, more friable, and often associated with bleeding, which does not fit the description of the tumor in the vignette.

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumor typically presents as a painful blue-purple nodule under the nail or on the fingertips, which does not match the location or description of the tumor in the vignette.

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: Hemangioma is typically a soft, compressible mass that may have a bluish discoloration, which does not fit the description of the firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor in the vignette.

rejected.label: Cavernous hemangioma
rejected.why: Cavernous hemangioma is a type of vascular malformation that usually presents at birth or early childhood and has a different pathological appearance than what is described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is a rare skin cancer that typically presents as a large, firm plaque or nodule, often with a history of slow growth over years, and its pathological features do not match those described in the vignette.
